correctness.rationale: There are exactly 14 S3-alphabet-label orbits of length-four ternary words, consisting of the forced constant orbit of size 3 and thirteen orbits of size 6. The 243 target words split into exactly 41 orbits, and the deletion-subsequence condition is invariant on each orbit. All 2,380 choices of fewer than six additional source orbits fail coverage; exactly 37 of the 1,716 choices with six additional orbits cover all targets, giving 39. Reversal fixes 5 choices and pairs the other 32. Two differently implemented exhaustive checkers reproduce all numbers and independently validate all 243 targets of a 31-word unrestricted witness. The proof derives completeness of the finite search and makes no assertion about the unrestricted optimum.

value.rationale: Global alphabet relabeling is a natural invariance of the insertion channel, so the cost of imposing it on the codebook is a motivated coding-design question rather than an arbitrary restricted sample. The theorem gives the complete exact symmetry-constrained optimum 39, all 37 labeled optimizers, and 21 reversal classes. A directly verified 31-word unrestricted construction proves a symmetry penalty of at least eight codewords; the gap reveals a substantive rigidity cost at the first nontrivial ternary length beyond a known three-symbol example.
